items.name: base
items.title: Hairline base
items.description: Hairline design tokens, the Tailwind theme and the type utilities. Use when installing any Hairline component — everything depends on it.
items.author: Hubert Formin <hformin@gmail.com>
items.docs: Import the Hairline theme once at the top of your global stylesheet: `@import "@hairline/tokens/theme.css";` — or copy the tokens in directly. Hairline sets font-variant-numeric on every figure; do not override it, and never set a figure in the sans inside a table.

items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.description: A pill button in four tones and three sizes. Use when the user takes an action; solid is the one primary action per view.
items.author: Hubert Formin <hformin@gmail.com>
items.docs: Exactly one `tone="solid"` button per view. Use `quiet` for the action beside it, `ghost` for tertiary, and `danger` only for destructive actions.

hairline.purpose: The one pressable shape in the system.
dontUseWhen: selecting from a set of options

insteadUse.navigating between pages: a link styled with buttonVariants via asChild

hairline.antiExampleWhy: Stock Tailwind palette colours are not Hairline tokens, the radius is not the pill the system uses, and "Submit" is not a plain verb naming what will happen.

items.name: icon-button
items.title: IconButton
items.description: A round button holding one 24-grid stroke glyph. Use when an action is clear from its icon and space is tight.
items.author: Hubert Formin <hformin@gmail.com>
items.docs: The `label` prop is required — a button holding only a glyph is unreachable without an accessible name.

dontUseWhen: the action needs a word to be understood
it is the primary action of a view
hairline.antiExampleWhy: No accessible name, and none of the system's sizing or tone tokens.

items.name: chip
items.title: Chip
items.description: An outlined pill holding a whole phrase. Use for suggestions, presets and filters — not for single words.
items.author: Hubert Formin <hformin@gmail.com>
items.docs: Set `interactive={false}` for a chip that only reports; it renders a <span> so it stays out of the tab order.

hairline.purpose: An outlined pill carrying a whole phrase.
hairline.antiExampleWhy: A chip holds a phrase, not a word; a one-word chip should be a button or a badge.

items.name: badge
items.title: Badge
items.description: A mono uppercase state marker in five tones. Use to mark the state of the thing it sits beside.
items.author: Hubert Formin <hformin@gmail.com>
items.docs: Ink and wash travel together — never a border-only accent, and never colour alone.

hairline.antiExampleWhy: Border-only accent, stock palette colour, and not the mono uppercase label the system uses for state.

items.name: tile
items.title: Tile
items.description: The only card shape: a fill, a radius, no border. Use to group anything that belongs together on a board.
items.author: Hubert Formin <hformin@gmail.com>
items.docs: Exactly one `tone="dark"` tile per page, holding the primary figure.

useWhen: grouping a figure with its meaning
hairline.antiExampleWhy: Cards in this system take a fill, never a border.

items.name: stat-block
items.title: StatBlock
items.description: A label, a big tight figure and one line of meaning. Use whenever a number is the point of a section.
items.author: Hubert Formin <hformin@gmail.com>
items.docs: Say the number, then say what it means: a `value` without a `note` is usually a missed sentence.

hairline.purpose: Presents a figure with its consequence.
dontUseWhen: a figure inside a table row
hairline.example: <StatBlock label="Total expenses" value="1 284 900" unit="XAF" note="258 900 of it is the deferred fees." />
hairline.antiExampleWhy: No label, no consequence, and a sans figure with comma grouping instead of the system's mono tabular figures.

items.name: data-row
items.title: DataRow
items.description: A ledger line: dot, name, mono meta, figure and running total. Use for any list of transactions or entries.
items.author: Hubert Formin <hformin@gmail.com>
items.docs: A settled or skipped line uses `state="demoted"` or `"struck"` — it steps down AND takes a mark, because lightness alone is not readable.

hairline.example: <DataRow dot="var(--a-coral)" name="School fees" meta="22 Mar · Mobile money" state="alarm" amount="−258 900" secondary="227 400" />
hairline.antiExampleWhy: Unformatted figure, no tabular alignment, and a table border model the system does not use.

items.name: meter-bar
items.title: MeterBar
items.description: A limit meter, or a stacked composition bar weighted by amount. Use to show a share or a spend against a ceiling.
items.author: Hubert Formin <hformin@gmail.com>
items.docs: Pass `over` when spend exceeds the limit; the component will not infer it, because the threshold is a policy decision.

hairline.purpose: Shows a proportion or a limit.
dontUseWhen: a precise comparison of many values
hairline.antiExampleWhy: Native progress carries browser styling the system does not control.

items.name: field
items.title: Field
items.description: A labelled value on a grey fill, with an optional prefix and hint. Use for any form input.
items.author: Hubert Formin <hformin@gmail.com>
items.docs: Use `size="lg"` for the single amount a form is about — never for two. Pass `editable` for a real input.

hairline.example: <Field label="Amount" size="lg" prefix="XAF" value="250 000" hint="Leaves nothing until the 28th." />
hairline.antiExampleWhy: A placeholder is not a label, and the field loses the system's fill, radius and figure treatment.

items.name: select-display
items.title: SelectDisplay
items.description: A closed dropdown trigger with an optional category dot. Use when showing a chosen value; it does not open a menu.
items.author: Hubert Formin <hformin@gmail.com>
items.docs: This is the trigger only — it renders the closed state and calls onClick. Wire it to your own popover, or use a native <select> when you need platform behaviour.

hairline.purpose: Shows a chosen value in the closed state.
useWhen: displaying a selected account or category
a trigger for your own popover
dontUseWhen: you need a working menu with keyboard selection
hairline.example: <SelectDisplay label="Category" value="School fees" dot="var(--a-coral)" meta="3 this month" />
hairline.antiExampleWhy: Fine as a trigger, but do not present it as a functioning select without wiring a real menu behind it.

items.name: toggle
items.title: Toggle
items.description: A switch, or a whole settings row with its consequence. Use for a setting that takes effect immediately.
items.author: Hubert Formin <hformin@gmail.com>
items.docs: Give it a `note`: a setting without its consequence stated is the most common copy failure in finance UIs.

dontUseWhen: a form field that needs saving
hairline.example: <Toggle on label="Round up every payment" note="Adds about 4 200 a month to the vault." />
hairline.antiExampleWhy: No consequence stated, so the user cannot tell what turning it on does.

items.name: segmented-tabs
items.title: SegmentedTabs
items.description: A grey track with one raised white segment. Use as the only tab pattern in the system.
items.author: Hubert Formin <hformin@gmail.com>
items.docs: Mono uppercase labels are the default. Use `mono={false}` only when a tab holds a phrase rather than a code.

hairline.purpose: Switches between a small set of views.
hairline.antiExampleWhy: Loses the raised-segment treatment that is the system's only tab pattern.
